findings.claim: The new `user != null` term in `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` reverses the old `context.getUser() == null` condition. As a result, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` no longer runs on the initial login page, where no user is set yet. Conditional passkey UI (`enableWebAuthnConditionalUI`) is therefore not set up for unidentified, first-time passkey login in `UsernamePasswordForm` and `UsernameForm`.

verifier.reason: UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-161 returns `webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so on the first login page (getUser()==null) the calls at :115 and :137 skip webauthnAuth.fillContextForm, which is what sets ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:43). The old code ran it exactly when the user was null; UsernameForm reaches the same path through the inherited authenticate/challenge.

findings.claim: `UsernameForm.authenticate` (line 47) calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration in `UsernamePasswordForm` now requires a `UserModel` parameter and has no zero-argument overload, so the call does not compile.

findings.claim: The test methods `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` and `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication` duplicate about 60 lines of code.

findings.claim: The webauthn-form absence checks in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest` (around lines 289-295 and 310-317) use `try { assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception)`. The inner assertion is dead code because `findElement` throws `NoSuchElementException` rather than returning null. Catching the generic `Exception` treats unrelated WebDriver failures as expected.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `try { MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) {}` at PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest (patch lines 542-547 and 563-568). `findElement` never returns null, so `nullValue()` can never pass, and `catch (Exception)` would also swallow unrelated WebDriver failures. One correction: the assertion is not fully dead code — if the form exists it throws an AssertionError, which `catch (Exception)` does not catch, so the presence case is still detected.

findings.claim: The new `user` parameter is only null-checked; the user's passkey credentials are never checked. During re-authentication, a user with no passkey is still shown the passkey form.

verifier.reason: UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-161 makes `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` return `webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so the user is only null-checked. During re-authentication (user set, lines 92-117 and 137-139), `fillContextForm` therefore always turns on ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI and the WebAuthn challenge (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:43; WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:85-121, where the conditional subclass's `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returns false at :65-67, so the user's WebAuthn credentials are never looked up). A realm with passkeys enabled therefore shows the passkey form to a user who has no passkey.

findings.claim: The `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` test disables passkeys for the whole realm via `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)` instead of testing a user without a passkey while passkeys are enabled.

verifier.reason: In the patch (change.patch:526-534), `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` calls `.setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, which turns passkeys off for the whole realm, so the case of a user without a passkey while passkeys are on is never tested. The comment at line 524 says this was intended, but the test name and the comment at line 555 ('as this user does not have passkey') describe the other scenario.
